name: Dark/Light Mode
description: Light, dark, and System themes: the saved choice applied in the head before the first paint, with storage that can fail; color tokens with a light and a dark value that set color-scheme; a radio group to choose; System that follows the system's setting live; and a control that stays in step after Back and across tabs.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Add or extend themes: Light, Dark, and System, saved under the app's storage prefix and applied by a short script in the head before the first paint; color tokens with a light and a dark value, and color-scheme set to match; a radio group to choose; System following the system's setting as it changes; and a control that stays in step with the saved choice. Build on the project's theme setup when it has one. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: The saved choice applied before the first paint, with storage wrapped in try/catch
Light, Dark, and System, with System following the system's setting live
Tokens with a light and a dark value, color-scheme to match, and theme-color
A radio group (or a menu of three) to choose, shown by the script
The control in step with the saved choice after Back and across tabs
Contrast in both themes, with a stronger border token for fields and controls
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, and any theme setup (projectDetection). If the project already has themes, extend them to meet this guide instead of adding a second system, and keep their API and storage key.
2. Add the script before the first paint (frameworkPatterns.themeBeforePaint, implementationDetails.beforePaint).
3. Set up the color tokens and color-scheme (implementationDetails.colors), and move components onto the tokens.
5. Check media, motion, and forced colors (implementationDetails.media, implementationDetails.motion, implementationDetails.forcedColors).
6. Check the result against testingChecklist in both themes, with both system settings, after Back, with a keyboard, and in forced colors, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

patternSpec.problem: Themes applied after the page paints flash the other theme on every load; choices get lost; form controls stay light on a dark page; borders that pass in one theme vanish in the other; and a toggle that cycles through three states hides what the next press does.
patternSpec.solution: Save Light, Dark, or System; apply it in the head before the first paint; color with tokens that have a light and a dark value and set color-scheme to match; offer the choice as a radio group; follow the system's setting under System; and keep the control in step with what's saved.
do: Apply the saved choice with a short blocking script in the head, before the stylesheets
Wrap storage in try/catch and fall back to the system's setting
Use tokens by purpose with a light and a dark value, and set color-scheme to the theme
Offer Light, Dark, and System as a radio group, or a menu of the three
Keep the choice in memory, so a failed save loses nothing; follow the system's setting live under System; and resync the control on pageshow and the storage event, a cleared storage included
Keep text at 4.5:1 and the borders of fields and controls at 3:1 in both themes
dont: Apply the theme in a framework's mount or effect
Store the choice under a bare key such as "theme" instead of the app's prefix
Use a button that cycles through three states
Use the 1.3:1 divider color for the borders of fields and controls
Invert colored logos with a filter
Animate a theme change under reduced motion
examples: Saved "dark" on a light system: dark before the first paint.
Saved "system", or nothing, on a dark system: dark, then light the moment the system switches.
Storage blocked in a sandboxed frame: the page follows the system's setting, and a choice holds until the page closes.

tokens.description: Suggested tokens by purpose, each with a light and a dark value; the project's tokens win. Contrast is against the background and the surface.

required.name: --color-border-strong
required.purpose: The borders of fields and controls, at least 3:1

preference.storageKey: The app's own prefix, such as acme.theme, or a cookie for server rendering

implementationDetails.beforePaint: A short blocking script, first in <head> before the stylesheets, reads the saved choice and sets data-theme="light" or "dark" on <html>. Applied later, in a framework's mount or effect, the other theme paints first. Reading storage can throw where it's blocked (a SecurityError in a sandboxed frame, in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, checked), so it's wrapped in try/catch, and the page then follows the system's setting. The script also sets <meta name="theme-color">, which colors the browser's toolbar on phones. Under a Content-Security-Policy it needs the page's nonce or its hash. Server-rendered apps put the script where the framework writes the head (Next.js: the root layout; Nuxt: app.head; SvelteKit: app.html). The attribute it sets differs from the server's HTML, so React needs suppressHydrationWarning on <html>; or the server reads a cookie and renders the right theme.
implementationDetails.colors: Colors are tokens by purpose (background, surface, text, muted text, border, strong border, accent), each with a light and a dark value, and components use the tokens, never raw colors. color-scheme: light dark on :root with light-dark() follows the system's setting even without script, and data-theme pins color-scheme to one theme, which also switches form controls and scrollbars (checked: an input's background in all three engines). light-dark() has been in every current browser since 2024; for older ones, repeat the tokens under [data-theme="dark"]. Contrast holds in both themes: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for the borders of fields and controls (1.4.11). Thin dividers can be lighter (#e0e0e0 is 1.3:1 on white), so controls get a stronger border token (#767676, 4.5:1). Check the project's own colors in both themes. Dark backgrounds are usually a dark gray, such as #121212, rather than black, and saturated colors are toned down; both are suggestions, and the project's palette wins. Tailwind follows the attribute with @custom-variant dark (&:where([data-theme=dark], [data-theme=dark] *)); in its CSS (version 4), or darkMode: ['selector', '[data-theme="dark"]'] in its config (version 3.4.1 and later).
implementationDetails.control: Three choices are a radio group (a <fieldset> with the legend "Theme") drawn as a segmented control, or a menu of three radio items. Two themes are one button with aria-pressed and a label that stays the same ("Dark theme"). A button that cycles through three states doesn't say what the next press does. Icons beside the words are decorative; with icons only, each option still has its name. A choice applies at once and holds for the page, which keeps it in memory; it's saved where storage works, so a save that fails, with storage blocked or full, loses nothing on the page. Under System, the theme follows the system's setting as it changes: a matchMedia listener fires in all three engines (checked). The control shows the saved choice at load, again on pageshow (after Back, Chromium restores the checked radio after the page's scripts have run, checked), and when another tab saves a choice or clears storage (the storage event, whose key is null after a clear). A page restored from the back/forward cache takes the saved choice only if what storage holds changed while it was away (a removed choice is a change, not saved System), so a choice that couldn't be saved isn't lost (checked in Chromium's back/forward cache). Without script, the control stays hidden, since it couldn't do anything. Choosing announces nothing more: the radio says its new state.
implementationDetails.media: Logos and icons need to show in both themes: an inline SVG with currentColor, a second asset, or <picture> with prefers-color-scheme sources, which follow the system's setting rather than the saved choice. filter: invert(1) suits single-color dark logos only; it turns an orange logo blue. Images with white backgrounds can sit on a surface, or be dimmed slightly in the dark theme. A favicon for dark tabs: <link rel="icon" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">.
implementationDetails.motion: Colors change at once. Elements with hover transitions also animate when the theme changes; if that looks wrong, turn transitions off for a frame while switching, with a class on <html>. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, a theme change never animates, View Transitions included.
implementationDetails.forcedColors: In forced colors, the system's colors replace the tokens. Nothing depends on a color or a background image alone, and the chosen option in the control takes Highlight.

requirements.1.4.1: The chosen option shows by more than color.
requirements.1.4.11: The borders of fields and controls, focus indicators, and icons meet 3:1 in both themes.

requirements.2.4.7: Focus indicators show in both themes.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version.

themeBeforePaint.description: The head script and the tokens: the saved choice read in try/catch, an unknown value counted as System, data-theme and theme-color set before the first paint; tokens with light-dark() and color-scheme: light dark, which follow the system's setting without script, pinned by data-theme. "acme" stands for the app's storage prefix.
themeBeforePaint.html:
<!-- First in <head>, before the stylesheets: the saved choice is applied before the first paint.
     "acme" stands for the app's own storage prefix. Under a Content-Security-Policy, the script
     needs the page's nonce or its hash. -->
<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">
<meta name="theme-color" content="#ffffff">
<script>
  (() => {
    let choice = 'system';
    try {
      choice = localStorage.getItem('acme.theme') ?? 'system';
    } catch {
      // Storage can be blocked; the page then follows the system's setting
    }
    // Light or Dark as chosen; anything else follows the system's setting
    const dark = choice === 'dark' || (choice !== 'light' && matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches);
    document.documentElement.dataset.theme = dark ? 'dark' : 'light';
    document.querySelector('meta[name="theme-color"]').content = dark ? '#121212' : '#ffffff';
  })();
</script>

themeChoice.description: The control: Light, Dark, and System as real radios drawn as a segmented control and shown by the script; a choice applied at once and kept in memory, saved where storage works, so a failed save loses nothing; System following the system's setting live; the control and the theme set again on pageshow; and the saved choice read again when another tab saves a choice or clears storage, and taken when the page comes back from the back/forward cache only if storage changed while it was away.
themeChoice.html: Theme

edgeCases.severalTabs: Several tabs: a choice in one applies in the others.
edgeCases.frames: Frames from other sites keep their own theme; pass it as a parameter where they take one.
edgeCases.chartsAndCode: Charts and code highlighting need their own colors in each theme.
edgeCases.darkOnly: An app that has only a dark theme sets color-scheme: dark and offers no control.

testingChecklist: The saved choice is applied in the head, before the first paint, so no load or reload shows the other theme first
Light and Dark apply as chosen; System, nothing saved, or a value the app doesn't know follows the system's setting

Where storage is blocked or full, nothing breaks: the page follows the system's setting or the saved choice, and a new choice holds until the page closes, also when the page comes back from the back/forward cache
Under System, the theme follows the system's setting when it changes, without a reload
The control offers Light, Dark, and System as a radio group or a menu of the three, or for two themes one button with aria-pressed; no button cycles through three states
The control shows the saved choice at load, after Back, and when another tab changes or clears it
color-scheme matches the theme, so form controls and scrollbars follow it, and so does theme-color
Without script, the page follows the system's setting and the control is hidden
Colors are tokens with a light and a dark value, and components use the tokens
Text meets 4.5:1 and the borders of fields and controls 3:1 in both themes; thin dividers may be lighter
Focus indicators show in both themes
Logos, icons, and images stay visible in both themes
In forced colors, the page uses the system's colors and the chosen option stays visible
Under reduced motion, a theme change doesn't animate
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens
